name: phase11_levers
rule: Every Phase 11 switch that changes detection / identity behaviour is decided by the rule registered here BEFORE its measurement (git history shows the order). Later work packages append their levers in their own commit, again before measuring.

amendments.approved_by: user (project owner), after the measurement below
amendments.change: on_if criterion 2: '0 false SUBMERSION in S1/S3/S4/S5' -> 'false SUBMERSION in S1/S3/S4/S5 ON <= OFF' (no net-new false alarm compared with OFF).
amendments.reason: Measured on the registered battery (evidence/wp1_identity_ab.json): the guard raises the S6 swim-over submersion 5/5 (OFF: 1/5). The only false SUBMERSION (S4 seed 103, two lane-2 swimmers passing within 0.1 m swap ids) occurs identically in all four arms, v2 included: a baseline artefact of position-only association, not caused by the guard. The absolute criterion let that baseline noise block a safety fix.
amendments.result_under_amended_rule: POOL_HANDOFF_GUARD ON; POOL_RANK_BY_DISTANCE OFF (exact tie on every criterion).
amendments.wp1_closure: still pending: the crossing-swap fix (its own lever, pre-registered before measuring) and the blind-band hand-off test for same-lane passing.

POOL_HANDOFF_GUARD.what: PoolTracker pure handoff (no other camera currently sees that global id) never links a new track into a camera that itself saw that person within HANDOFF_GUARD_S of their last sighting: that camera's own (v2) resurfacing logic owns the person. Overlap matches are unchanged.
POOL_HANDOFF_GUARD.why: Development observation (seed 0-4 probe, before this rule): with live cross-camera identity, a swimmer re-acquired 0.4 m from where another person had just gone under inherited the submerged person's global id in 2/5 seeds, so no vanished-swimmer watch opened and the SUBMERSION was MISSED; per-camera (v2) operation raised it 5/5. A safety regression: it must be fixed in WP1.
on_if: S6 swim-over drill: the submerged person's SUBMERSION is raised within 10 s of the vanish in 5/5 battery seeds, AND
AMENDED 2026-10-09 (see amendments[0]): false SUBMERSION in the full-coverage scenarios S1, S3, S4, S5 (all seeds) ON <= OFF - the guard adds no net-new false alarm compared with OFF
POOL_HANDOFF_GUARD.original_on_if_2: 0 false SUBMERSION in the full-coverage scenarios S1, S3, S4, S5 (every seed)
POOL_HANDOFF_GUARD.otherwise: STOP WP1 and report with numbers (the guard cannot be left OFF while S6 misses a submersion).

POOL_RANK_BY_DISTANCE.what: PoolTracker ranks overlap and handoff candidates together by distance / gate. v2 ranks EVERY overlap match (within OVERLAP_GATE_M of a person another camera sees now) above every handoff match, however much closer the handoff is.
POOL_RANK_BY_DISTANCE.why: Development observation (blind-band probe, before this rule): an instructor re-acquired 0.05 m from their own predicted position took the global id of a child standing 0.82 m away (seen 0.43 s earlier by another camera): an id swap between two different people.
on_if: over S1-S5 (all seeds): handoffs kept / handoffs ON >= OFF, AND
shared-global-id frames (two different people under one id at the same time) ON <= OFF, AND
missed and false SUBMERSION (as defined below) not more than OFF
POOL_RANK_BY_DISTANCE.tie: A tie on every criterion is NOT a win: the lever stays OFF.

POOL_ID_REPAIR.registered: 2026-10-09, before any implementation run or measurement
POOL_ID_REPAIR.what: After each camera's PoolTracker update (live/identity.py LivePoolTracker): a local track whose global id A is seen by another camera, at the same time, more than REPAIR_SPLIT_M (2.0 m) away, while exactly ONE other global id B is seen by another camera within OVERLAP_GATE_M of this track (and B is not on another track of this camera), is re-linked A -> B after REPAIR_MIN_UPDATES (5) consecutive such updates - only if this camera's link to A is YOUNGER than the conflicting cameras' links to A (the older consensus wins; no oscillation). It never links to an id nobody sees now.
POOL_ID_REPAIR.why: Battery result (evidence/wp1_identity_ab.json, all arms): two lane-2 swimmers passing within 0.1 m (S4 seed 103) leave one person under two ids (cam1/cam2 vs cam3/cam4); when that person leaves cam3/cam4 the id 'vanishes' -> false SUBMERSION; S4 also has 440-743 shared-id frames per seed from the same swaps.
POOL_ID_REPAIR.decided_with: POOL_HANDOFF_GUARD ON, POOL_RANK_BY_DISTANCE OFF (decided, amendment a4a90f8)
POOL_ID_REPAIR.seeds_note: Fresh: never run before this registration.
POOL_ID_REPAIR.scenarios: S1-S6 as in battery, plus S7
POOL_ID_REPAIR.S7: blind band (13 m range) same-lane passing: two lane-3 swimmers swimming towards each other (0.9 m/s each) meet in the middle of the 3.8 m band nobody sees, and both are handed off on the far side; + an overtake in lane 2 (0.6 / 1.2 m/s) + swimmers in lanes 1 and 4; 75 s
on_if: over S1-S7 (all seeds): shared-global-id frames ON < OFF (strictly fewer), AND
handoffs kept / handoffs ON >= OFF, AND
false SUBMERSION ON <= OFF and missed SUBMERSION ON <= OFF (S6 still 5/5), AND
POOL_ID_REPAIR.wp1_closure: WP1 closes only if, with the decided configuration, S7 (all its seeds) keeps 100 % of the scripted handoffs and raises 0 false SUBMERSION. Otherwise STOP and report with numbers.

RESPONSIBILITY_GATING.registered: 2026-10-09, before any measurement (there is no measurement of it on this laptop: the simulation rig produces no behaviour alerts)
RESPONSIBILITY_GATING.what: A behaviour alert from a calibrated camera NOT responsible for the person's pool spot (live/responsibility.py: in view, >= RESP_MIN_PX_PER_M (25) px per metre there and >= 1/RESP_DENSITY_RATIO (1.25) of the best camera's density) is recorded and linked but does not sound ('deferred to <camera>') while a responsible, MONITORED camera sees the same global id. Never: SUBMERSION, FAULT, ghosts, people without a global id, or when no responsible camera sees the person (fail-safe).
RESPONSIBILITY_GATING.measured_by: WP6 site session on the client server: offline replay of the synchronised 4-camera drill recordings D1-D7 plus the normal-session recording, each arm on the same recordings
on_if: false alarms per camera-hour (normal session) ON < OFF (strictly fewer), AND
every drill alert that sounds in OFF has a sounding alert for the same person (global id) in ON - 0 drill alarms lost, D5 submersions 10/10 in both, AND
time to the first sounding alert per drill ON - OFF <= 0.5 s
RESPONSIBILITY_GATING.until_measured: OFF. The laptop gates of WP2 (projection round trip, identical membership, responsible coverage) do not decide it.

MULTIVIEW_CONFIRM.what: A detection with score >= MULTIVIEW_MIN_SCORE whose pool position (box bottom-centre through the camera's calibration) lies within OVERLAP_GATE_M of a person ANOTHER calibrated camera of the pool sees right now (pool tracker), and where this camera has no confirmed track yet, is born and confirmed at once (ByteTrack confirm_now) instead of waiting for the next frame / the birth threshold. Never on uncalibrated cameras; never creates a second track where this camera already tracks someone.
MULTIVIEW_CONFIRM.decided_by_wp3_spec: the pre-registered A/B on the held-out split (eval/heldout_v1, TEST split, criteria order of eval/heldout_v1/split.json). The held-out split has NO multi-camera clip (10 single-camera stock clips): the switch cannot act there, so this A/B is necessarily an exact tie and a tie is not a win -> OFF. Run anyway as a no-regression check: ON must be bit-identical on every clip.
MULTIVIEW_CONFIRM.re_decided_at_site: WP6 site replay of the synchronised 4-camera drill recordings (D1-D4, D6), each arm on the same recordings, pool level: ON iff time_to_first_detection_s median AND p95 ON <= OFF with at least one strictly lower, AND track_breaks_per_person_minute ON <= OFF, AND false alarms per camera-hour (normal session) ON <= OFF, AND no false SUBMERSION added, AND same-camera duplicate ids = 0. Otherwise OFF.

DET_TILING_REGION.what: When DET_TILING is on, tiles cover only the camera's RESPONSIBLE region (live/responsibility.py, projected into the view) instead of the whole frame / water ROI; tiles are counted at the real frame size (2560x1440 at this site) for admission.
DET_TILING_REGION.default: 'responsible' - it has no effect while DET_TILING stays 'off' (Phase 8 decision, eval/heldout_v1/levers_phase8.json)
DET_TILING_REGION.decided_with: DET_TILING itself, at the WP6 site session (capacity at 15 fps with tiling off and on + in-water recall): DET_TILING is switched on only if the site capacity admits all 4 cameras at 15 fps with it AND in-water recall rises; this lever is not measured on its own.

GLARE_HOLD.registered: 2026-10-09, after a disclosed design probe (below) and BEFORE implementation runs or the A/B
GLARE_HOLD.design_probe: docs/phase_reports/phase11/WP3.md: through the real PersonTracker + scene, the CURRENT code keeps the id through straight glare passes up to 3.5 s with no false SUBMERSION, and a true vanish in glare raises SUBMERSION 5.2 s after the loss; it switches id on a fast 4.5 s pass (+ a false SUBMERSION) and on a fast turn inside the glare.
GLARE_HOLD.what: A glare mask per camera (auto: persistently saturated low-saturation pixels, EMA over frames; plus operator GLARE zones drawn on the camera) split into regions. A track lost INSIDE a glare region is HELD for at most GLARE_HOLD_MAX_S: a new track born from that same region within the hold takes the held track's id - only if exactly ONE track is held in that region and no other track entered it since. The submersion watch is untouched: it opens and counts from the real loss time exactly as without the hold (a link only resolves it as any resurfacing does).

battery.rig: synthetic box streams (2560x1440, 15 fps) through the real PersonTracker + SceneBehaviorTracker (whole frame = water), glare region a rectangle in the auto mask; box jitter 2 px, 5 % missed detections
battery.seeds_note: Fresh: never run before this registration (the probe used seed 0, no misses).

scenarios.G1: straight passes, glare 1.5 / 2.5 / 3.5 / 4.5 s x speed 60 / 150 / 300 px/s
scenarios.G2: turn inside the glare (comes out the side it entered), glare 1.5 / 3.0 s x speed 60 / 300 px/s
scenarios.G3: stops 2 s inside the glare, then swims out (glare 1.5 s of travel)
scenarios.G4: true vanish inside the glare (never comes out)
scenarios.G5: SAFETY: person A vanishes inside the glare; 1.5 s later person B (never seen before, entering the glare from the far side) comes out of it
scenarios.G6: two people enter the glare 1 s apart and both come out

metrics.id_kept: the person keeps one public id from before to after the glare (G1-G3, G6 per person)
metrics.false_submersion: a SUBMERSION for a person who came out of the glare
metrics.missed_submersion: G4 / G5: no SUBMERSION for the vanished person within 10 s of the loss

on_if: missed_submersion ON = 0 over G4 + G5, all seeds (G5 is the case the hold could make worse), AND
G4 submersion_delay ON - OFF <= 0 s on every seed (the hold never delays the alarm), AND
id_kept ON > OFF over G1-G3 + G6 (strictly more people keep their id)
GLARE_HOLD.held_out_check: If ON by the battery: the held-out TEST split (eval/heldout_v1) must not lose event recall or gain false alerts with it ON, else OFF (the auto mask is active on real footage).
GLARE_HOLD.re_checked_at_site: WP6 D7 glare-pass drill replay with the decided value: report track breaks during glare and SUBMERSION outcomes; if it misses a D5/D7 submersion the lever is switched OFF.

battery.rig: tests/integration/_pool_sim.py: 4 calibrated corner cameras (pinhole, 5 m, ~90 deg, aimed 8 m along the centre line from their own end), 15 fps, runtime-wide clock, cameras not frame-synchronised; real per-camera live path (calibration -> calibrated WATER zone -> PoolIdentity.bind -> scene ingest / score / expire -> identity.stamp)
battery.seeds_note: Not used by any run before this registration (development probes used seeds 0-11).

scenarios.S1: full coverage (17 m range): swimmers lanes 1-4 (one lap clip shifted in pool space) + instructor & child 0.7 m apart (lane 5) + one true vanish mid-pool at 30 s; 75 s; px noise 1.5, miss 4 %
scenarios.S2: blind band (13 m range; nobody sees a 3.8 m band across the centre): swimmers lanes 1-4 + instructor & child; 75 s
scenarios.S3: S1 with px noise 3.0 and 10 % missed detections
scenarios.S4: crowd: 12 swimmers (3 per lane 1-4, starts 9 s apart) + instructor & child (14 people); 75 s
scenarios.S5: overtake: two swimmers in lane 2 (0.6 / 1.2 m/s) + swimmers lanes 3-4; 75 s
scenarios.S6: swim-over drill: a person goes under for good at (6.0, 3.75) at 20 s; a swimmer occluded from 18.5 s to 21.5 s resurfaces 0.4 m past that spot; + swimmer lane 4; 40 s

metrics.handoffs: every new local track of a person who already had a global id; kept = its first global id is the id the person last carried
metrics.shared_gid_frames: frames in which two different people carry the same global id (any cameras)
metrics.duplicates: (camera, frame)s with one global id on two tracks of that camera
metrics.missed_submersion: a scripted vanish with no SUBMERSION fire from a watch on that person's track within 10 s
metrics.false_submersion: a SUBMERSION fire from a watch on a person whose longest all-camera unseen gap is < 3.0 s (TRACK_STALE_SECONDS) - people occluded for longer are not counted (no camera can tell)

metrics_wp3.time_to_first_detection_s: per ground-truth person: (first annotated frame where a CONFIRMED predicted track (track_id >= 0) matches the person's box) - (first annotated frame where the person is visible (vis != invisible) and in a monitored state (in_water / edge)), in seconds; a person never matched counts as 'missed' (reported separately, not as a time). Summaries: median, p95, n, missed. Resolution is the annotation spacing (reported).
metrics_wp3.track_breaks_per_person_minute: (id switches + fragmentations of the matched confirmed track over the person's monitored annotated frames, as ClipDetectionTracking.tracking counts them) / (sum over persons of (last - first monitored annotated frame) / fps / 60)
metrics_wp3.per_camera_and_pool: Single-camera: per clip. Multi-camera site recordings: per camera, and pool-level where the person is matched in ANY camera (a pool-level first detection is the earliest over the cameras).

gates_wp5.registered: 2026-10-10, after the disclosed planning measurements below and BEFORE any WP5 code; plan + deviations 1-3 approved by the product owner 2026-10-10
gates_wp5.baseline: dev laptop (RTX 4060 Laptop GPU, driver 610.74, ORT 1.19.2, real RTMDet-m dynbatch on CUDA), warm OS file cache, 2 admitted 2560x1440 H.265 1 s-GOP cameras over MediaMTX, API killed and restarted (tests/_stack harness): process start -> health ready 5.80 / 5.84 s; -> all cameras MONITORED 8.97 / 9.03 s (+ 2 s NSSM AppRestartDelay). Capacity sweep (batch 1..8) 3.1 s of it. Cold OS cache (first profile of the day): imports 8.6 s + provider guard 13.3 s. Guard and runtime already share ONE ORT session (deviation from the plan item 'one model load instead of two': a regression test, no code).

cache.cached: the GPU batch-latency table only (batch_ms 1..batch_max); the per-frame CPU overhead is re-measured at every start
key: GPU name + uuid + driver version (nvidia-smi; CPU: processor name + core count)
cache.unknown_gpu_identity: cache not used for that start (measure)
cache.corrupt_or_unreadable: ignored with a warning, full measure, file rewritten; never blocks startup

spot_check.what: on a key hit: median of 5 batch-1 runs after the guard's warm-up, compared with the cached batch-1 latency
spot_check.else: full batch 1..batch_max sweep before any admission, cache rewritten
spot_check.why_asymmetric: admission keeps HEADROOM = 0.9 (10 %): a GPU more than 10 % slower than the cache would over-admit; a faster GPU only wastes capacity (re-measured beyond 30 %). Deviation 1 (approved): replaces the plan's +-30 %. Measured batch-1 run-to-run spread 15.0-16.8 ms (about +-6 %).

gates_wp5.warm_up: cache hit: batch sizes 2..min(N enabled cameras, batch_max) get one warm-up run each before admission (the guard already warmed batch 1). Cache miss: the full 1..batch_max sweep is kept (deviation 2, approved): latency per frame RISES with batch size on the dev GPU (15.0 -> 17.6 ms/frame, batch 1 -> 8), so extrapolating unmeasured sizes would over-admit.

gates.G1: process start -> every enabled camera admitted <= 10 s (warm restart, cache hit; dev laptop GPU run, the test's own timeline)
gates.G2: capacity phase on a cache hit (spot check + warm-up 2..N) <= 0.6 s
gates.G3: warm crash recovery: process start -> all cameras MONITORED, reported against the 8.97-9.03 s baseline (same rig, 2 cameras); not a pass/fail number (deviation 3, approved: ~60 s is not reproducible on a warm restart)
gates.G4: a cache hit admits exactly the cameras a full measurement admits (same limit)
gates.G5: a spot check outside the tolerance, a key mismatch, a stale or a corrupt cache each force the full measurement

gates_wp5.fps_fallback: camera_fps_fallback (default 15): an implausible stream fps (outside 1..240, e.g. 90000) uses it instead of 25; fps_source 'fallback' in the capture status + a WARNING (approved option (b) of WP4 finding 4.2)

gates_wp6.registered: 2026-10-10, BEFORE any WP6 code and before any site recording; plan + decisions 1-5 approved by the product owner 2026-10-10

decisions.1_minors: No minors in ANY recording (drills and normal session). D6 is run with adults only (an instructor + adult learners with floats / noodles). The kit refuses to record until the operator attests 'no person under 18 in the water or in view' for that recording; the attestation is logged.
decisions.2_normal_session: A separate gated step `record --normal --hours N` (adults-only session, >= 1 h per camera; 4 camera-hours minimum for a rate). Same legal gate as the drills. If the client declines it, every rule needing it stays PENDING and the lever stays at its shipped default.
decisions.3_replay: Lockstep 'replay' source through the real LiveRuntime (recorded session clock, no frame drops, no camera more than one frame period ahead of the slowest analysed camera) + detection record/replay keyed by (camera, frame, call) with an input digest: the first arm runs the GPU, later arms reuse its exact detector output; a digest mismatch aborts the arm.
decisions.4_tiling_capacity: Capacity with DET_TILING on is COMPUTED from the batch-latency table the running API measured (CapacityProfile with calls_per_frame = 1 + tiles at 2560x1440), never by restarting or stopping monitoring.
decisions.5_report: Two stages: PROVISIONAL (on the day: rows computable from the drill log, the live run and the replay traces) and FINAL (after the 1 fps box labels and the alert review). A row whose inputs are missing is PENDING, never PASS.

legal_gate.before_any_recording: DPIA reference, data-sharing agreement reference, counsel approval reference, retention period, signage up (yes), performer consent forms on file for every performer id (yes), adults-only attestation (yes). Empty / 'no' -> recording refused. References are recorded in session.json, never the documents.
legal_gate.storage: DataDir\site_session\<id>\ with SYSTEM + Administrators only (inheritance removed); RIGHTS.csv rows (DATA_PROTOCOL 8) with rights_status 'pending' until the agreement is countersigned

drills.SYNC: a light flash (or clap) visible to every camera; mark = the flash. Used to measure inter-camera offset (> 2 frames -> measured offsets applied in the replay, reported)
drills.D1: 6-15 adults spread over all lanes, 3 min (marks: start, end)
drills.D2: ONE adult swims 25 m lengths through every camera handoff, 4 lengths, alone in the water (lifeguard on deck) (marks: start, end)
drills.D3: entries one at a time by adults: step in, ladder, jump (a mark at each entry)
drills.D4: zone crossings: lane changes and on/off the submerged teaching platform, 1-2 adults (marks: start, end)
drills.D5: controlled submersion: a trained adult sits on the bottom 10-15 s with a rescuer in the water; 10 runs spread over the far end of every camera and the overlap areas (marks: under, surfaced)
drills.D5b: WP3 safety finding: as D5, and a second adult swims past in the ADJACENT lane within ~2 m, 2-5 s after the performer goes under - never over the performer (marks: under, pass, surfaced); >= 5 runs
drills.D6: standing adult instructor + adult learners with floats / noodles in shallow water, 5 min (false-alarm check; ADULTS ONLY)
drills.D7: glare-zone passes (afternoon light): an adult swims through the glare region repeatedly, 3 min; optional D7s = one controlled submersion inside the glare (lifeguard's decision) (marks: start, end / under, surfaced)

criteria.status: PROPOSED pass levels (Phase 11 plan table); the client confirms or changes them as an amendment of this file BEFORE the session - never after any result is seen

C1a_in_water_recall.stage: FINAL (box labels on 1 fps sampled frames, IoU >= 0.3)

C1b_analysed_fraction.pass: >= 0.99 on every camera at 15 fps, MONITORED throughout, 0 dropped
C1b_analysed_fraction.source: 5-min live run with all enabled cameras

C2a_handoff_retention.definition: lone-swimmer drill (D2; D4 when one adult): a handoff = an in-water observation of the swimmer by a camera that did not see them in the previous 1.0 s; kept = its global id equals the swimmer's id just before
C2a_handoff_retention.stage: PROVISIONAL (D2); FINAL adds multi-person drills from labels

C2c_incidents_per_person.pass: 1 incident per D5 / D5b run (the performer's global id)

C3a_time_to_first_detection.definition_provisional: entry mark -> first confirmed in-water track (new global id) within 10 s; resolution of the mark ~0.5 s
C3a_time_to_first_detection.stage: PROVISIONAL (event level); FINAL = the WP3 metric time_to_first_detection_s on labels

C3b_track_breaks.pass: <= 0.5 per person-minute AND 0 false SUBMERSION in D2/D4/D7
C3b_track_breaks.definition_provisional: lone-swimmer drills: (distinct global ids - 1) per in-water minute
C3b_track_breaks.stage: PROVISIONAL (lone swimmer + false SUBMERSION); FINAL = WP3 metric on labels

C3c_submersion.pass: SUBMERSION for the performer <= 10.0 s after the 'under' mark in 10/10 D5 runs

C3c_D5b_watch_clearing.pass: reported: SUBMERSION for the PERFORMER (not the passer) <= 10.0 s after 'under' in every D5b run; any miss confirms the WP3 safety finding on site and becomes a pre-registered lever proposal (no automatic change)

C4_false_alerts.inputs: every alert in D6 is false by construction; normal-session alerts need the reviewer's verdict (review sheet)
C4_false_alerts.stage: FINAL (PENDING without the normal session or its review)

levers.target_analysis_fps: stays 15 iff the 5-min live run has every camera MONITORED throughout, analysed fraction >= 0.99 and 0 dropped at 15 fps; otherwise C1b FAILS and the report lists the options (fewer cameras per GPU, a stronger GPU, cameras at a lower fps with re-validation). Never lowered automatically.
levers.DET_TILING: PROVISIONAL: computed capacity with tiling (decision 4) must admit every enabled camera at 15 fps; FINAL: in-water recall ON > OFF on the labelled D1+D6 frames (detector-only, same frames). Both, else off. DET_TILING_REGION follows it.
levers.RESPONSIBILITY_GATING: the WP2 rule as registered (63f90c3), on the replay arms OFF vs GATING; needs the reviewed normal session -> FINAL; PENDING without it
levers.MULTIVIEW_CONFIRM: the WP3 site rule as registered (e595224), on the replay arms OFF vs MULTIVIEW; needs labels -> FINAL
levers.GLARE_HOLD: decided OFF in WP3; D7 replay with OFF: track breaks during glare and SUBMERSION outcomes reported
levers.tie: a tie is not a win: the shipped default stays

replay_arms.pinning: each arm is a COMPLETE thresholds values set written by the kit (every Phase 11 switch explicit), so a later default change cannot alter an arm
replay_arms.detector: the OFF arm records every detector call; GATING and MULTIVIEW replay them (identical input digest required)

session_checks.camera_check: per camera vs docs/CAMERA_SETUP.md: codec hevc, 2560x1440, measured fps 15 +- 0.5, keyframe gaps all 1.0 s +- 1 frame over >= 2 GOPs in a 20 s window (irregular -> 'H.265+ / dynamic GOP' FAIL), no B-frames, frame-rate timing present (else WARN), hardware decode (else WARN), first frame <= 3 s
session_checks.coverage: every 0.5 m pool cell has >= 1 responsible camera; all cameras calibrated to ONE pool; overlap band reported
session_checks.capacity: tiling off from the running API's measured table; tiling on computed (decision 4)
session_checks.sync: inter-camera offset from the SYNC flash <= 2 frames, else measured offsets applied

gates_wp7.registered: 2026-10-10, BEFORE any pre-open code (git history shows the order). Design written first; gates fixed here.
gates_wp7.work_package: WP7 follow-up 3: open the cameras in parallel with the provider guard and the capacity phase
gates_wp7.approved_by_product_owner: 2026-10-10 (WP5 follow-ups 1-3 approved; 'do all the changes' for the WP7 plan incl. its recommendations: identical-admission meaning, A/A arm)
gates_wp7.baseline: WP5 gates_wp5: 2 admitted 2560x1440 H.265 1 s-GOP cameras over MediaMTX, API hard-killed + restarted, capacity cache hit: all MONITORED 6.22-6.75 s after process creation (tests/integration/test_fast_restart_gpu.py). OpenCV serialises RTSP opens process-wide, ~1.8 s each.

design.idea: a closed-gate CaptureWorker is opened right after database_ready, in parallel with threshold audit, provider guard and capacity phase. Frames are read and DISCARDED (keeps the TCP session drained); nothing is queued, no CameraWorker / detector / recorder / identity binding exists. After admission (profile.admit, unchanged) the runtime ADOPTS the matching pre-opened capture: attaches the stream clock and the queue, builds the CameraWorker + detector, then opens the gate.
design.what_is_pre_opened: enabled RTSP cameras in admission order (name order); never file / replay sources (eval harness unchanged); only when live runtime is enabled and camera_preopen is on
design.adoption_key: (camera id, decrypted source, source type); any mismatch (source edited, camera disabled) stops the pre-opened worker and opens a fresh one as today
design.release: PreOpener.close() stops every un-adopted worker: capacity-refused, invalid source, disabled, startup refused. Called at the end of LiveService.start(), in start_live's failure path and in the lifespan finally; idempotent; stop signalled to all first, then one shared join budget; a blocked OpenCV open releases its capture when the open returns (CaptureWorker.run finally); preopen_max_hold_s=60 stops anything never adopted
design.switch: camera_preopen (AQUAGUARD_CAMERA_PREOPEN); default decided by the rule below
design.admission_meaning: required_fps() counts the observed fps of admitted cameras that already have a frame. Today camera 1 usually has no frame yet when camera 2 is admitted (a race); with pre-open it always has one. 'Identical admission' therefore means: identical for every camera whose fps <= target_analysis_fps (the site: 15 = 15). For a camera faster than target the pre-open admission is deterministically the stricter, documented rule; a unit test pins it. Alternative (hiding pre-admission fps) rejected: it would keep a race on purpose.
design.api: additive only: capture status 'preopened' flag, timeline events preopen_started / preopened per camera. No migration.

gates.P1_speed: WP5 rig, 5 restarts per arm, arms alternated ON/OFF in the same run (laptop GPU heat hits both). PASS iff median(ON all-MONITORED after process creation) <= median(OFF) - 1.0 s AND every ON sample <= 10 s (WP5 G1 still holds). Also reported against the WP5 baseline 6.22-6.75 s. A restart whose spot check re-measures is kept and counted in its arm, flagged.
